questions.question: A number line runs from 0 to 1 and is divided into 100 equal parts, so each small step is one hundredth. Point A sits on the 30th mark from 0, which is the decimal 0.3. Point B sits on the 25th mark from 0, which is the decimal 0.25. Which statement is true?
options: 0.3 is greater, because 0.3 is 30 hundredths and 30 hundredths is more than 25 hundredths
0.25 is greater, because it has more digits after the decimal point
0.25 is greater, because 25 is bigger than 3
Point A and Point B are the same distance from 0
questions.explain: On a line cut into 100 equal parts, 0.3 lands on the 30th mark and 0.25 lands on the 25th mark, so 0.3 is farther right and greater. The common trap is thinking the longer decimal wins; give both numbers the same number of places (0.30 and 0.25) and compare hundredths.

questions.question: A number line runs from 0 to 1 and is divided into 100 equal parts, so each small step is one hundredth. Point C sits on the 80th mark from 0, which is the decimal 0.8. Point D sits on the 55th mark from 0, which is the decimal 0.55. Which point is closer to 1?
options: The point at 0.55, because 55 is a bigger number than 8
The point at 0.8, because 80 hundredths is closer to 100 hundredths than 55 hundredths is
The point at 0.55, because having two decimal places makes a decimal bigger
Both points are exactly the same distance from 1
questions.explain: The whole is 1, which is 100 hundredths, so count hundredths: 0.8 is 80 hundredths and 0.55 is 55 hundredths, and 80 is nearer to 100. The trap is comparing 55 with 8 as if they were whole numbers instead of rewriting 0.8 as 0.80.

questions.question: A number line runs from 0 to 1 and is divided into 100 equal parts, so each small step is one hundredth. Three points are marked: the 9th mark is 0.09, the 45th mark is 0.45, and the 50th mark is 0.5. Which list puts the three decimals in order from least to greatest?
questions.explain: Rewrite every decimal with two places (0.09, 0.45, 0.50) and order the hundredths: 9, then 45, then 50, which matches the marks from left to right on the line. The trap is treating 0.5 as small just because it has only one digit after the point.

questions.question: Ali draws a number line from 0 to 1 divided into 10 equal parts and marks point X on the 4th mark, which is 0.4. Bea draws her own number line from 0 to 1, the same length, divided into 100 equal parts, and marks point Y on the 40th mark, which is 0.40. Which statement is true?
options: 0.40 is greater than 0.4, because 40 is greater than 4
0.4 is greater than 0.40, because tenths are bigger pieces than hundredths
0.40 is greater than 0.4, because it has more digits
0.4 and 0.40 are equal, because 4 tenths is the same amount as 40 hundredths
questions.explain: Each tenth is made of 10 hundredths, so 4 tenths equals 40 hundredths and both points land at the same spot on the line. Adding a zero at the end of a decimal never changes its size, so a longer decimal is not automatically bigger.

questions.question: Which of these decimals is the greatest? 0.68, 0.7, 0.65, 0.09
questions.explain: Compare the tenths place first: 7 tenths beats 6 tenths and 0 tenths, so 0.7 is greatest, and writing it as 0.70 makes it clear that 70 hundredths is more than 68 hundredths. The trap is picking 0.68 because it has more digits.

questions.question: Which comparison is TRUE?
questions.explain: Line up the places and check tenths first: 3 tenths is less than 4 tenths, so 0.35 < 0.4 (or 0.35 < 0.40 in hundredths). The trap is judging by how many digits a decimal has, which wrongly makes 0.35 look bigger than 0.4.

questions.question: In gym class at a Surrey school, four students record their standing long jump: Jonah 0.9 m, Maya 0.85 m, Priya 0.78 m, Sam 0.8 m. Who jumped the farthest?
options: Priya, 0.78 m
Maya, 0.85 m
Jonah, 0.9 m
Sam, 0.8 m
questions.explain: Rewrite each jump in hundredths: 0.90, 0.85, 0.78, 0.80, so 90 hundredths is the longest jump. The trap is thinking 0.85 beats 0.9 because it has more digits.

questions.question: In art class four paint jars hold 0.8 L, 0.45 L, 0.6 L, and 0.09 L. Which list orders the amounts from least to greatest?
questions.explain: Write each amount with two decimal places (0.80, 0.45, 0.60, 0.09) and order the hundredths: 9, 45, 60, 80. The trap is sorting the one-digit decimals first as if fewer digits meant a smaller amount.

questions.question: Ava and Liam pick blackberries near Chilliwack. Ava's container holds 0.7 kg and Liam's holds 0.65 kg. Ava says her container holds more. Liam says his holds more because 65 is bigger than 7. Who is correct, and why?
options: Ava, because 0.7 kg is 70 hundredths of a kilogram and 70 hundredths is more than 65 hundredths
Liam, because 0.65 has two decimal places and 0.7 has only one
Neither one — the two containers hold equal masses
Liam, because 65 is greater than 7
questions.explain: Before comparing, give both decimals the same number of places: 0.7 kg becomes 0.70 kg, and 70 hundredths is more than 65 hundredths, so Ava has more. The trap is reading the digits after the point as whole numbers, which makes a longer decimal look bigger.

questions.question: At a skating rink in Kamloops, four students race one lap. Their times are Owen 12.5 s, Mia 12.45 s, Zoe 12.54 s, and Leo 12.6 s. The fastest skater is the one with the shortest time. Who is the fastest?
options: Owen, 12.5 s
Mia, 12.45 s
Zoe, 12.54 s
Leo, 12.6 s
questions.explain: First remember that the fastest skater has the smallest time, then write every time in hundredths (12.50, 12.45, 12.54, 12.60) and pick the least, which is 12.45 s. The trap is assuming 12.45 must be a large time because it has more digits than 12.5.

questions.question: Which number can go in the blank to make this statement true?  0.4 > ____ > 0.29
questions.explain: The number must be less than 0.4 and greater than 0.29, so compare in hundredths: 0.35 is 35 hundredths, which sits between 29 and 40. The trap is checking only one side of the statement, or thinking a decimal like 0.9 is small because it has just one digit after the point.

questions.question: At a store in Victoria, Sasha compares two juice boxes: one holds 0.25 L and the other holds 0.3 L. She says the 0.25 L box holds more because 25 is bigger than 3. Which statement best explains the correct answer?
options: Sasha is right, because 0.25 L has more digits, so it holds more
Sasha is right, because 25 hundredths is more than 3 hundredths
Sasha is wrong: the two juice boxes hold exactly the same amount
Sasha is wrong: 0.3 L is 3 tenths, which is 30 hundredths, and 30 hundredths is more than 25 hundredths
questions.explain: The 3 in 0.3 sits in the tenths place, so it means 30 hundredths, which is more than the 25 hundredths in 0.25. The trap is comparing 25 and 3 as whole numbers instead of matching the decimal places first.
